title: The Nottingham Corpus of Early Modern German Midwifery and Women's Medicine, ca. 1500–1700 (GeMi, OTA 2562)
notes: Whitt's GeMi corpus (Oxford Text Archive 2562, published 2016) holds 12 German midwifery and women's-medicine texts ca. 1500–1700 (Rösslin's Rosengarten, the anonymous Frauenbüchlein ca. 1500, Rüff's Trostbüchlein, HoffWeheMutter, HebammenBuch...) as paired plain-text and TEI XML files plus a manual. Transcriptions derive mostly from the Würzburg 'Digitale Volltexte' Gynäkologie collection; CC BY-NC-SA 3.0. The record is now held on the Oxford Text Archive's repository server (llds.ling-phil.ox.ac.uk); the older ota.ox.ac.uk/desc/2562 address no longer works, and the repository shows a bot-check page before the record in a browser. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the Renascor Corpus snapshot v2026.06 (texts harvested from this edition, duplicates included; they may cover only part of it).
institution: University of Nottingham (Richard J. Whitt), deposited at the Oxford Text Archive (ota:2562)
